entries.question: How is JAMB scored?
entries.answer: JAMB (UTME) has 4 subjects, each scored out of 100, for a total out of 400. English is compulsory. Your score is based on the number of correct answers — there's no negative marking for wrong answers, so always attempt every question.

entries.question: What is the UTME cut off mark
entries.answer: The UTME cut-off mark is the minimum JAMB score needed to be considered for admission. JAMB sets a national minimum (often 140-160), but each university and course can set its own higher cut-off. Always check your specific school and course's requirement.

entries.question: Explain photosynthesis simply
entries.answer: Photosynthesis is how plants make their own food. Using sunlight, water (from the soil), and carbon dioxide (from the air), plants produce glucose (sugar for energy) and release oxygen as a byproduct. It mostly happens in the leaves, in a part of the cell called the chloroplast.

entries.question: How can a student start earning online
entries.answer: Low-cost ways students can start earning: 1) Freelance a skill you already have (writing, design, data entry) on sites like Fiverr or Upwork. 2) Sell a digital skill locally via WhatsApp status/status ads. 3) Affiliate marketing — promote products and earn commission. 4) Offer a service to fellow students (typing, tutoring, phone repairs). Start with what needs zero capital first.

entries.question: How do I price my first gig
entries.answer: For your first gig: research what others charge for the same skill and start slightly below that to attract your first clients and reviews. Don't go too low — undervaluing makes it hard to raise prices later. As you gain reviews and experience, raise your price every few clients.

entries.question: What can this bot do
entries.answer: BUKASON helps with two things: Academics (JAMB/WAEC/NECO help, explaining school topics) and Business (low-capital ways to start earning as a student). Switch modes from the menu, and ask anything in plain language.
